print_methodology_body: This report summarizes the outputs of a Risk Wise scenario, which combines hazard data, exposure, and vulnerability functions to estimate annual expected losses. Inputs and configuration are recorded as SHA-256 hashes so the run can be reproduced from the same data on the same platform. Results — including the waterfall decomposition and any cost-benefit measures shown above — were generated by the CLIMADA engine via the Risk Wise pipeline.
print_reproducibility_note: Results are reproducible on the same OS/hardware with the same seed. Cross-platform results may differ by ≤0.01% in AAL.
print_section_hazard_description: This section summarizes the climate hazard configured for the scenario, including the hazard type and time horizon used to drive the risk calculation. Hazard intensities are sampled from CLIMADA hazard sets and projected to the future year under the selected climate scenario. Snapshots inserted below highlight the spatial pattern of the hazard for the present and future periods.
print_section_exposure_description: This section describes the exposure layer used in the scenario — the assets, populations, or other elements at risk that are exposed to the hazard. Exposure values are taken from the configured dataset and scaled by any annual growth factor over the time horizon. Snapshots inserted below visualize the exposure distribution across the affected geography.
print_section_impact_description: This section reports the impact of the hazard on the exposed assets, expressed as an annual expected loss for the present and future years. The waterfall chart decomposes the change in loss between the two years into its drivers (climate change, economic growth, and other configured factors). The table that follows lists each driver's contribution in the measurement unit returned by the engine.
print_section_cost_benefit_description: This section evaluates the adaptation measures configured for the scenario by comparing the cost of each measure with the avoided loss it produces over the time horizon. The cost-benefit chart visualizes each measure's footprint; the table lists every measure with its cost, benefit, and benefit-cost ratio (BCR), sorted by BCR so the highest-leverage measures appear first.
